artifacts.summary: Research on bootstrapping specs/ state and runtime-file ignore rules for fresh consumer repos: state-write.sh --init refuses the default state.json path by design, six call sites need the new init call, specs/tmp writer identified, and check-runtime-file-tracking.sh's tracked-file detection (item h) already appears satisfied by existing code.

memory_candidates.content: scripts/state-write.sh's --init mode unconditionally refuses (exit 1) to target the default live specs/state.json path (realpath-normalized comparison) as a deliberate guard against a filter typo destroying live task state. --init is only usable for explicit non-default targets like specs/archive/state.json. Any future 'bootstrap a fresh state.json' script must write that file directly rather than through state-write.sh.

check-runtime-file-tracking.sh's Check A (git check-ignore -q per probe path) already honors any applicable .gitignore at any directory depth, including a specs/-local specs/.gitignore -- no logic change needed to support ignore coverage delivered from a file other than the repo-root .gitignore, only messaging updates.

check-runtime-file-tracking.sh's Check B (tracked-ephemeral-file scan via git ls-files against RUNTIME_FILE_B_REGEX) already fails independent of .gitignore coverage -- it was rewritten onto the shared lib in commit 8695facc8 (task 201, 2026-09-09), predating a later task spec that assumed this detection still needed to be built. When a task description says a check 'must' do something, verify current behavior first -- it may already be shipped.
